questions.q: Why does Lesson 15's domain-routing Script Include depend on this lesson's integration existing?
options: Routing reads a caller's sys_domain value, which is only correct if that caller's sys_user record was synced and domain-tagged in the first place
It doesn't -- routing works whether or not sys_user records are synced
The routing script calls the Prairie View API directly, bypassing sys_user entirely
Flow Designer requires a live integration to be installed before any flow can run
questions.explain: getAssignmentGroupForCaller() assumes caller.getValue('sys_domain') is already correct -- that only holds once this lesson's sync has written a correctly domain-tagged record.

questions.q: Why is a scheduled pull chosen for Prairie View's integration instead of an inbound webhook?
options: Webhooks are against ServiceNow platform policy
Scheduled pulls are always faster than webhooks in every integration
Prairie View's homegrown, PeopleSoft-based module has no webhook or event-notification capability -- only a read endpoint exists
St. Catherine's and Lakeshore require Prairie View to also use their exact pattern
questions.explain: There's no event to receive from a system that was never built to call out -- a scheduled pull against its read endpoint is the only realistic option.

questions.q: What does `PrairieViewWorkerSync.pullChangedWorkers` do when the REST call returns a non-200 status?
options: It retries immediately in a tight loop with no delay
It logs the failure with `gs.error` and returns an empty array, rather than passing an unverified response into the upsert step
It throws an unhandled exception that crashes the scheduled job
It silently returns the raw error body as if it were worker data
questions.explain: A bad response is logged and never allowed to reach the upsert logic -- the same "never pass through what you haven't verified" discipline from this track's error-handling lesson.

options: It stores the assignment group for the worker's tickets
It's only used for St. Catherine's and Lakeshore, never for Prairie View
It's a display label with no functional purpose
It's the coalesce field -- the check that lets a repeated or retried sync update an existing record instead of creating a duplicate
questions.explain: Querying on this field before deciding insert vs. update is exactly the upsert/coalesce pattern this track's Retry Strategies & Idempotency lesson taught, applied here to people instead of tickets.

questions.q: Why doesn't this lesson also build St. Catherine's Workday integration and Lakeshore's ADP Workforce Now integration in full?
options: Because those two integrations are not part of Technical Architecture's approved plan
Because Workday and ADP cannot be integrated with ServiceNow at all

Because they follow the exact same pull/coalesce/domain-tag template as Prairie View's, just against more modern APIs -- building all three here would repeat the same lesson without teaching anything new
Because St. Catherine's and Lakeshore were deferred out of Phase 1 entirely
questions.explain: This lesson proves the integration template against the hardest case -- a homegrown system with no modern API -- rather than repeating the same shape three times.
